audit.whatIsWrong: The page invents an Olaf ability called 'Vicious Strikes' and repeats it in nine places, always as 'true-damage autos'. It also claims Ragnarok converts his autos to true damage, calls Tough It Out his lifesteal, and describes his true damage as percentage-based.
audit.why: Olaf's real kit: Berserker Rage (P) gives attack speed and lifesteal scaling with MISSING health; Undertow (Q, 9s, 1000 range) reduces armour and move speed and RESETS its cooldown if he picks the axe up; Tough It Out (W, 16-12s) is attack speed plus a shield, no healing; Reckless Swing (E, 11/10/9/8/7s, 325 range) is the true damage and it costs him health; Ragnarok (R, 100/90/80) is passive resists plus immunity to disables while he keeps attacking — it adds no damage conversion. His autos are not true damage at any point.
audit.corrected: Every 'Vicious Strikes' reference replaced with the correct source: Undertow for the slow/shred, Reckless Swing for the true damage, Berserker Rage for the lifesteal. Ragnarok claims narrowed to the stun, per the mirror.
sources: enemyKit Riot text, all five slots

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 3, 5 and 6 read Skill / Skill / Olaf in both layers.
audit.why: Packet chart and the already-audited mirror both have Olaf / Olaf / Skill. The matchup's own whys agree: whys[3] calls 4-5 his peak, whys[5] says he still edges the first-item stage, whys[6] describes genuine parity at two items.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 5, 6 flipped as matched pairs in both layers with ratings moved to follow.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ragnarok's cooldown appeared once in prose but not at the level-6 spike, and Undertow's reset was never mentioned anywhere.
audit.why: The axe reset is the reason his slow feels permanent — walking over a thrown axe hands him another one immediately, which is what actually denies your charge window.
audit.corrected: Added the reset to whys[3], early and mid; Ragnarok's 100s put on the level 6 why.

edits.before: At level 1 Olaf throws an axe to slow you, then walks in for Vicious Strikes autos that deal true damage your W-shield cannot reduce. Do not try to charge a full Q while slowed — his auto-attack speed under W beats your charge time. Farm with partial Q taps from max range, keep the wave slightly frozen toward your tower, and deny him free poke angles by standing behind the minion line. Your W-shield is not wasted early; pop it defensively to stay healthy, not offensively to trade back.
edits.after: At level 1 Olaf throws Undertow to slow and shred your armour, then steps in for Reckless Swing — 325 range, true damage, and no resist of yours reduces it. Do not charge a full Q while slowed; his attack speed under Tough It Out beats your charge time. Farm with partial Q taps from max range, keep the wave slightly frozen toward your tower, and never walk over a thrown axe: picking it up resets Undertow instantly. Pop W defensively to stay healthy, not offensively to trade back.

edits.before: At level 4-5 Olaf gains access to his full combo and his Ragnarok cooldown is fresh every fight, so every trade you initiate risks burning your charged-Q stun into a CC-immune brawler who out-sustains you. Save the fully charged Q for the gap between his Ragnarok casts — when the icon is grey, that is your all-in window. Your E shreds his armor and sets up the Q stun, but only commit that sequence when Ragnarok is definitively on cooldown. Level 6 gives you Unstoppable Onslaught to disengage or chase, but it does not flip the lane — it just opens roam options if you are even.
edits.after: At level 4-5 Olaf has his full combo and Ragnarok is fresh every fight, so every trade you start risks burning your charged-Q stun into a champion who ignores disables while he keeps attacking. Save the fully charged Q for the gap between Ragnarok casts (100s at rank 1) — when the icon is grey, that is your all-in window. Roar of the Slayer shreds his armour and sets up the stun, but only commit that sequence with Ragnarok down, and never chase over a thrown axe: picking it up resets Undertow. Level 6 gives you Unstoppable Onslaught to disengage or chase, but it does not flip the lane.

edits.before: Once Heartsteel has 200+ stacks and you have a tank mythic, your HP pool grows large enough that Olaf's true damage per auto is a smaller fraction of your total and your zombie passive becomes a genuine zone threat. The 49% win rate reflects this near-parity — neither of you dominates the other cleanly at full build. Play for teamfight engage with Unstoppable Onslaught, target the squishies behind Olaf rather than trying to out-duel him 1v1, and your W-shield plus zombie form give you enough staying power to anchor the frontline even if he wins the isolated skirmish.
edits.after: Once Heartsteel has 200+ stacks and you have a tank mythic, your HP pool grows large enough that a Reckless Swing hit is a smaller fraction of your total and your zombie passive becomes a genuine zone threat.
